lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: I'd like to call this meeting to order. Welcome here, everyone. And at this time, I would like to give the opening to Councillor Jake Hiebert.

lines.speaker: Jake Hiebert
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jake Hiebert (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. A recent prominent concern of the citizens of this city is the perceived influx of homeless people and the visibility of their possessions. I'd like to preface this opening by saying this council is aware of the issues and is working to address them. There were— are 12 or so people that frequent the old vacuum cleaner property as well as the property behind Lettingham Car Dealership. I've made it a point to stop by each day for the past 2 weeks and dialogue with these individuals, all of whom have a name. These individuals are the first to admit that caring people who drop off food are providing a temporary fix. Communal housing is not what they are seeking. They identified their needs as being long-term places to live, A job, mental health and drug addiction intervention, along with immediate medical care. Methamphetamine appears to be the drug of choice among these homeless. Some of the homeless women are struggling with previous rapes and abuse. Communal housing is frowned upon. We must realize that homeless people struggling with mental health and drug issues don't trust each other. They would rather live in an area with 2 or 3 persons that they can trust. People who will not steal their drugs, their money, or their recently acquired possessions. This past week I heard that several of the homeless people have stolen from others and now have moved out. On Saturday, there were only 4 people left in the vacuum cleaner property encampment. I could be convinced that places that provide food and people envisioning an overnight shelter on cold nights have the best of intentions. They care for the homeless person as an individual. However, this is not what the homeless are identifying to me as a need. Feeding the homeless is making everyday life a little better and may very well extend their life on earth. In Steinbach, we're expecting people to overdose— are we expecting people to overdose on fentanyl, laced meth, and cannabis? In Canada, 47— just over 47,000 persons since 2016 have died of overdoses. Vancouver last year had 10,500 deaths. from overdoses, which is up by 34%. The people in our encampments, in my opinion, require long-term drug and mental intervention followed by housing and employment. Some of the homeless talked to prior to homelessness were carpenters, masons, they ran fairly large companies, and— or they were truck drivers. This last week I had an opportunity to tour a second-stage housing complex in Winnipeg called the Transitional Supportive Recovery housing facility in Winnipeg run by the Riverwood Church near Stadacona and Telva. This is an $8 million facility. After drug treatment and intervention, these homeless tenants are assisted in finding employment and independent housing. I learned that homeless people from Steinbach have been utilizing this facility and building structure in their lives while living there. In doing my research, I'm convinced that the homeless need to be introduced to places and facilities where there is help available. Steinbach does not have such adequate resources. Once a homeless community is built and exists, it requires infrastructure and resources, including professional medical people, drug treatment, social services, extra policing, healthcare intervention, sanitary facilities, et cetera. Again, similar to Teen Challenge, long-term drug treatment is the answer for the homeless struggling with addiction. Others require mental health intervention along with medication. People may say I don't have a handle on what's happening. Fair. If council remembers in my opening several months ago, I spoke about experiencing the homeless in Winnipeg as a young police officer in the early '70s. Since then, I have spent 39 years in policing, including Vancouver Drug Section, undercover assignments where I lived with drug dealers, users. I was a judge for prisoners at Stony Mountain. Order. I spent 6 years on the Parole Board of Canada interviewing prisoners applying for release, including drug users and dealers. I recently resigned from the Government of Manitoba Vulnerable Abuse Registry after 6 years, and now I'm on my 4th year sitting on the Provincial Government Criminal Code Review Board. This board is chaired by a judge and includes a psychiatrist and me as a layperson. Here we are— here we deal with individuals that through drugs and mental illness often committed heinous crimes. Subsequent to being convicted, a judge determined them to be unfit to stand trial or found them criminally not responsible at the time of the offense. Most of these individuals suffer from schizophrenia and/or mental issues often induced by drugs. I've been involved in over 50 years in public safety. I want the citizens of this community to know that this council again is aware of the issues and is determining the best solutions to deal effectively with homeless in our community. I recently read a book called Crooked Smile, where the writer, a 10-year drug abuser in Los Angeles Skid Row, lived homeless, did whatever he had to do to get drugs, and saw his many acquaintances on the street overdose and die. According to this writer, the answer to homelessness is not safe injection sites Or food or shelter. To have drugs at his disposal was the everyday priority of this drug user. In closing, I would like to read one paragraph or partial paragraph from the book where the writer, after being convicted on felony charges, states this: The proper deal should have been the opinion of no felony charge after mandatory year-long job placement. Thank you. So what he's saying is, the best thing for people, especially after his felony charge, should have been a long year, at least a 1-year-long placement. That would have been the truly progressive approach that I hope the rest of society is on the brink of discovering, but it might take a few more years of utter failure to convince the more stubborn. Then he goes on, I'm not talking about drug court, I'm not talking about 20-day, 28-day human warehouse facility. I'm talking about comprehensive, publicly funded, long-term treatment centers that equip the formerly addicted with a reasonable shot at prosperity. Psychiatric services, permanent care for those that are mentally unfit, and specific skilled training that feeds people directly into the trades and labor market. Thank you. lacking fields of industry. Some of the probab— some of you probably think I'm dreaming, he says, but you may be in for a surprise before the end of the decade. It all depends on how many more bodies those in power are willing to ignore. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor, and for members of council. This public hearing is to consider the file, variance file V-2024-12, for a property with a civic address of 322 Reimer Avenue in Steinbach. Both the owner and the— of the property and the applicant for the variance Yes. The applicant for this variance is 613-5367 Manitoba Inc. Purpose of the variance is twofold. First of all, to permit a detached accessory building to have a total size of 1,232 square feet, whereas single-family dwellings and their accessory uses within the C-2 commercial community zone may have a maximum size of 700 square feet. That the proposed accessory structure have a maximum height of 29.5 feet, whereas City of Steinbach zoning bylaw permits a maximum height of 15 feet. The applicant, as I mentioned, is proposing to construct a detached garage on the rear portion of the subject property. Notices, as are required by the Planning Act, have been issued. There is no written correspondence on file. Thank you. With respect to the proposal, the subject property does contain an existing 2-story structure with the lot having dimensions of 80 by 195 feet. A site plan was not provided by the applicant at the time of writing of this report. Administration has also provided council with Several precedent files where various accessory structures of sizes that actually exceed the proposed structure have been approved. However, administration would also like to point out to council that the proposed structure is intended to have at least a portion of the area as a second story, which we believe gives rise to the request of the height variance as well. With respect to the application, council will need to review and consider whether or not there may be detrimental impacts to the neighborhood. And in any event, should council choose to approve This particular application, administration also recommends that the application also be subject to the city's approval of a proponent-provided lot grading plan for the subject property.

And I asked him, you know, if you ever If you ever want to sell your house, please let me know, 'cause it was always special to me. I had heart surgery when I was 4 years old, and I have some photos of myself biking down that road and carried my hockey bag to the Centennial. It was a special property for me, and I didn't want to see it bulldozed. And I was fortunate enough to have my dad here today. He works with me, and— to move him into that house, which is kind of cool, 'cause I live out in the country, so I never intended to live there myself, but— I wanted to restore the home. We've already done a new roof on it. We have plans to refurbish the exterior with like a plaster so that it actually still looks like the old house that it was. It was a unique architecturally designed house from, I think, the '40s. So it's pretty cool. However, the one negative about this house is it is on an 80-foot— I thought it was 82, but 80-foot lot. Very wide, but yet they built the house wide, not deep. So the garage, me and my dad were joking about it, it's like a— almost like a lean-to. It's a lean-to. It kind of seems a bit like an afterthought when they built the house. I don't know if it was actually built after, but it's not even big enough to fit a regular-sized car, never mind an SUV or truck. So it really has basically no garage. We— he has like a little bit of storage in there, kind of like a shed, but unfortunately there's not really room, or it doesn't make sense to, to tear it off because it's so close to the side. You can, you can drive past it, but other than that, there's like— you'd have to tear it off to even have like a small Small oversized single garage, and then you couldn't get to the backyard. So that's why we would like to build this garage to have storage for my, my car, a car that I have that I don't want to park on gravel, and, and my dad's vehicle, motorcycle, stuff like that. There's no plan to do any, like, suite in it or anything. Just want to have a second story for— have the ability to have extra storage and a space up there. for me and my dad to use. And that's, that's about all I want to share.

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. This— given the events of the last 24 hours, thought it prudent for administration to provide council with a bit of an update as the city has experienced a pretty significant storm over the last Yes, Okay. So, as you're aware, we've had a significant amount of rain over the last day or so. It started the evening and night of Monday, September 16th, and into this morning with rainfall being intermittent until around mid-afternoon. According to media reports, a total of approximately 6 inches of rain fell in Steinbach and area during this period. And due to the saturated ground conditions and the amount of rain that fell, especially during this morning, the city experienced We experienced significant overland stormwater flows in all neighbourhoods. The city's open drainage channels, creeks, and ditches throughout the city were either at capacity or over capacity, with some spilling over their banks. And as the storm intensified, the stormwater flood pump at the city's main lift station on Park Road West began operating at 9:00 a.m. today, and it continues to be in operation until the sewer system flows return to normal ranges. This flood pump capacity is at 485 liters per second. And levels— I just got an update from the city's waterworks manager. The levels within the city's sewer system are still exceeding normal, and it's expected that that flood pump will continue operation Yes. And that was into later this evening. All of the city's lift stations were functional and pumping at full capacity during the storm event, and overland stormwater flows impacted many city roads, with particular note Park Road East, McKenzie Avenue, and Grandview Drive being some areas where the streets were actually overtopped, and that's where they where they cross the existing creeks within Steinbach. Many of the city's peripheral gravel roads were also impacted, and 16 washout areas have been identified by staff as of the end of today. And the T.G. Smith Centre site experienced some overland flooding with water entering the building this morning. Unfortunately, as a result, the ice surface has been lost. The ice-making process must start over, with the ice expected to be restored and be playable in about 2 weeks. And if staff are able to make it happen more quickly, they will certainly try to do so. City staff are continuing to work into the evening and to tonight to monitor and maintain the city's facilities until normal operations can be restored. It may take several days. Thank you. for administration to conduct a full assessment of the impacts on city facilities and infrastructure, and also more significantly, to determine the number of residential or other private properties affected by either overland flooding or sewer backups.

lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Michael Zwaagstra (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. In the month of August, we had just over $2 million in building permits issued, just under $1.3 million in residential and $750,000 in commercial. And so the year to date to this point is $53 million, so a strong year overall. And we're looking forward to seeing what happens in the rest of the year.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you. Anything further?

lines.speaker: Damian Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Damian Penner (Councillor) [medium]
lines.text: No further comment.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay. Anything further, council? Nothing closing? Nope. Okay. Council, yes, I think, yeah, August might have been— it might slow down a little bit, but all in all, it's still a very good year and there's still many projects that are getting talked about that are coming in the future. We did add a couple of dwelling units, 5, for a total of 156 dwelling units for the year so far. So that's a pretty good number. Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried.

lines.speaker: Michael Zwaagstra
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Michael Zwaagstra (Councillor)
lines.text: Mr. Mayor, I need to step out for this one, conflict of interest.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay, thank you. We've got 9D. This is rezoning bylaw 22. This is referring to 33 Loewen Boulevard. This is first reading. This will initiate a public hearing down the road. Mr. Warting, could you please introduce this file?

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. This particular application under bylaw 2250 is a rezoning application with the owner of the property The applicant for the proposed bylaw being Steinbach Bible College, Inc., with the applicant for the proposed bylaw being [name withheld]. Purpose of Bylaw 2250 is to rezone the subject property from C-4 commercial regional to EI educational institution— institutional to allow for the relocation of the Steinbach Bible College. located at 333 Loewen Boulevard, and it's the site of the former Steinbach Family Medical Center. The recommendation from administration is for council to give this bylaw first reading, and if first reading is approved, then a public hearing could be scheduled for October the 15th.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay, thank you, Mr. Warkentin. Council, how would you like to proceed?

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor)
lines.text: Motion to approve.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Second by Councillor Hiebert. Go ahead.

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. This is a building, the former Family Medical Centre, as stated, has been empty for 3, 4, maybe 5 years since we built the new medical centre on Stone Bridge Crossing. So this has been empty and in need of a tenant or a new owner. It's been— it's gone through a number of different owners with different plans. The latest one now is the Steinbach Bible College, which is, which is great that somebody wants to use that building and they need to repurpose it. And they also want to change the zoning from C-4 to educational institutional. So we need to pass first reading, then we can go to public hearing and hear what the neighbours and other people in Steinbach have to say about it.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you. Anything further?

lines.speaker: Jake Hiebert
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jake Hiebert (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. Yes, I agree with what Councillor Siemens has just said. It's nice to see the old medical building again being refurbished and being reused. And it's nice to see that this will now be changed to an educational facility and zoning, and we're going to have students there, we're going to have housing there. I just think it's a great, great building and use in that area, which is largely residential. So I'm excited that it's been purchased and looking forward to the renovations.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further? Yes, Council, that has been a property that's been empty for some time. It's been empty ever since we had the new care clinic, doctor clinic And I think too, I'm looking forward to this. I want to see what the people, the public will say, the neighborhood. There have been different times that property's come to council for different reasons and different uses. And just excited to see what could happen maybe with this property now. And just, I love the public hearing process because we get to hear From the residents, and that's, that's what's great. Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. So we're looking forward to— that was October 15th-ish?

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Yes, that's the anticipated date of the public hearing.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you very much. Okay, council. Council question period. Are there any questions of council? Councillor Zwaagstra.

lines.speaker: Michael Zwaagstra
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Michael Zwaagstra (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. I'm sure that other members of council have heard from the public on this one as well, and that is in regard to the encampment on Main Street. Councillor Hiebert, of course, made reference to it in his opening, and the universal feedback that I've heard is that there's significant concern regarding the safety for the people in the area. The businesses and frankly for the people who have been in the encampment themselves. And so I would like to put it out there as a question to our, to our city manager in terms of, is there any information that he has that, you know, that any that has come to the city in regards to this? And I'd also like to put it out to council. Is there something— do we want to, you know, look into some options in regards to our bylaws What type of mechanisms might be at our disposal? What do other cities do in regards to dealing with this challenge? Because even when this particular property is, is addressed, we know that the issue will, will come, will come up elsewhere because it's clearly unacceptable. We cannot have people simply encamping in, in, in areas like that in Steinbach. It's not safe, not appropriate, and that's the universal feedback that I've heard from people, and I, I agree with that feedback. So I just wanted to put it out there to our city manager in terms of is there any information in regards to that, you know, in terms of the city's— has received in regards to this and to council, is there any steps that we're looking to potentially take?

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Thank you, Councillor Zwaagstra. Just for council's information, through the past several years, The City of Steinbach has been involved on a case-by-case basis on several different locations of homeless encampments within Steinbach. In all cases, city staff that have been part of any interaction We have dealt with several groups. Primarily, it starts with the property owner. The city has also been in contact with the RCMP and also with a variety of nonprofit agencies and social support agencies that are operating in Steinbach. And that does sometimes change. Involvement does vary from time to time, but it's It always is evaluated on a case-by-case basis. With respect to the particular location that Councillor Zwaagstra referred to, that is a site of a former business property in Steinbach on Main Street at 447 Main Street, did— was impacted by a building fire earlier this year. Thank you. Yes. And the property still sits in its state since the fire, and the building has not been torn down. There has been an encampment that was first noticed sometime in August. City's understanding is that the property owner and other individuals who have been connected with that property have been attempting to deal with the issue. As I understand it, the owner or individuals acting on behalf of the owner did serve a formal trespass notice to all of the individuals that were present on the property as of September 5th. And it is my understanding that as of Monday, September 16th, That all individuals had left or otherwise vacated that property.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay, thank you. Go ahead, Councillor Stevenson.

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. I appreciate the effort here to understand the role of council and really the— or the city in the homeless situation. And that That begs a couple of questions. Is what is the role of City Council in this? When we get phone calls, and we've all had phone calls to do something about it, and I agree we need to do something about it, but what is it that we do? At FCM in Calgary, at our national conference, we dealt with that issue. We saw firsthand the issue in Calgary, and so it's, it's an issue that's across our nation, not Just in our community, but it does affect us here too. So what's the— then the question is, what's the role of the city, the city of Steinbach and City Council within this? Our job here is basically is under the Manitoba Act that we work under. We are responsible for infrastructure, for parks, we're responsible for policy and bylaws and zoning, community plans, long-term plans. And is this a social issue that we have to now deal with, start to be involved with? How many tax dollars do we put towards social? issues. We do have a lot of good social services in Steinbach that are run through donations and various organizations, including our churches. We have strong organizations in Steinbach that provide a lot of support. One of the roles of council also is to put protection into place, and we have that. We have that with our RCMP. We also have that with a bylaw inspector who enforces our bylaws and various things. So I appreciate the fact that we ask administration for, for a review and, and a follow-up to this, which will start a discussion at City Council, but maybe also a community discussion as part of it when it is released. So I think I'm very much in favor of getting administration to begin the process. Okay.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further? Anything, anything to add?

lines.speaker: Michael Zwaagstra
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Michael Zwaagstra (Councillor)
lines.text: Yeah, thank you, Mr. Mayor. So just to be clear, I mean, one of the things that, that I've, you know, certainly heard reports of is that when people are dropping off, you know, food and donations there, that is not the most helpful thing people can do. If you want to help, you know, we've heard this consistently from many different organizations, Donate to the organizations that are actively working with at-risk people who actually know how to target it better. So donate to good organizations such as Steinbach Community Outreach, Helping Hands, Soups On, you know, you know, if we want— in terms of just, in terms of more immediately, if people want to donate individually, that is a far better way to donate than to— because we don't want these encampments to continue. And so what I'm looking for in regards to— because we can't ask our staff, they're not going to solve this problem, they're not going to come up with, with a solution here. But in terms of, you know, giving some information to council in regards to, you know, what are some of the potential tools that council could have, like, is— what are some of the bylaws, for example, that other municipalities have in place addressing these types of encampments? And is there something we can learn from some of these other municipalities in regards to what, what they do? And so that's the kind of direction that I'm hoping to go, because even again, it's good to hear that You know, this, this one has been mostly or entirely vacated, but we know that the issue will come up again in the future and we need to be prepared to deal with it.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Yes, you know, Council, I do agree and I, I respect and I thank that we, that we have administration that is, that is working on this and that we have a community safety officer that is going out there and and working with the homeowner, the property owners, and working with the RCMP to resolve the issues that are there. But what I would ask is that we ask our administration exactly as Councillor Zwaagstra has said, to look into it to see what other communities are doing. I would actually like to, for what to come out of this is actually a policy that we can follow. Thank you. 'Cause that's what we do. We set policy as we were told by Councillor Siemens, and that is one of the things we do. We do city planning. This is part of, I believe this is part of our planning. And it would be nice to have a policy, and I'm not saying that we have to put, like, we don't put money into social programs, but that we have a policy to deal with these that we can have, and this is, this is the way we go, and we already do. They already go through that way and through the certain avenues, and it does always start with the property owner. But I would like to have, I think, a documented written policy. Mr. Warden, do we have a written policy on this at this time?

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: No, there is no specific direction, certainly not one process that's been approved by council. As maybe in my own mind, I referred to it in my earlier comments, but in general, city administration has to date approached this particular matter as it's a community-based issue. It's not a City of Steinbach as an organization issue. There are many factors related to homelessness, and it can run an extremely broad range of specific issues that the city has no knowledge of, experience of, or expertise in dealing with. That is up to, again, a community-based group approach that involves the property owner, the RCMP, and most importantly, the social service agencies who have the expertise and the experience that are able to best able respond to the particular issues surrounding this particular matter. What the City of Steinbach, through its administration, tries to do is be a facilitator to, if nothing else, try and get the appropriate resources together so that the issue can be at least— or sorry, at least an attempt can be made to resolve an issue. As we have seen more recently, it's something that is continuing to perpetuate, and it's an extremely difficult problem to find a solution for.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay, thank you. Yeah, that— you know what, thank you for your comments. Thank you. Thanks, Mr. Warkentin. And I agree, it is— they're case by case. Each one is individual. Each encampment is different, and they need to be dealt with individually as well. But council, do you— is there consensus for what Councillor Zwaagstra is asking, that we get— that we just have administration look at what other communities What other communities are doing so that we can figure out where we stand, what we need to do as a community. And I think that might be the best. So, Mr. Warkentin, I would put that on you and your administration and then to report back to us. And then, yeah, just so we can get some feedback. We also want to help the people in our community, and what is the best way? And I do believe Councillor Zwaagstra said it as well. I think it's best to donate or give to the organizations that deal with the concerns that are there. We don't know what we're dealing with. We mean well, but we don't know what we're dealing with. And I think it's best to go through an organization. Thank you. If these people are to be helped, I think they need to be helped by an organization that understands their needs and what they need to be— what needs to happen. Okay, thank you very much.

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: We've got 11A, correspondence and petitions. We have a letter from the Manitoba Consumer Protection and Government Services. This is referring to Canada Community Building Fund. CCBF allocations. Council, how would you like to proceed? Take his information? Yes, please. And we've got 11B. We have a letter from Harv's Err. This is referring to the SLI tower, the tower proposal. Council, we've all read the letter that he's He has written, he's asking us to write a letter in support to relocate the tower or the height, change the height, as it causes danger for his pilots. Council, how would you like to proceed? Councillor Zwaagstra.

lines.speaker: Michael Zwaagstra
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Michael Zwaagstra (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. I'll put a motion forward, and if there's a seconder, then I'll speak to it. And the motion is very simple, that the City of Steinbach write a letter expressing expressing support for the concerns raised by Harv's Air regarding the location of this tower.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay, do we have a seconder? Councillor Penner. Go ahead, Councillor

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor) [medium]
lines.text: Penner.

lines.speaker: Michael Zwaagstra
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Michael Zwaagstra (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. When we first received the information that this cell tower was going in place, that was all the information that we had. And again, this is not something that is initiated by the City of Steinbach. Obviously, this is well outside of our jurisdiction in that regard, but we do get notified as part of the process. Okay. And I think it's important to note that Harv's Air is a very busy airport, a very busy flying school. They're a respected business in our area, and they're— they, as noted in the letter here, they train a lot of pilots, they have a lot of planes, and they have some significant concerns regarding the location of this tower. The tower's height is significant, and this is right in their flight circuit, and they're concerned about safety. Safety. And this is the kind of thing that I really hope that Transport Canada takes seriously when this information is forwarded to them. I think by the City of Steinbach adding its voice to the concern and just that, you know, where we send them a letter saying that we recognize the importance of their business and that we urge the federal government, Transport Canada, to take these concerns seriously and into consideration, I think that is something that we should do as a city in regards to supporting supporting a local business that plays such an important role in our area. So I— that's why I think we should send the letter.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you. Anything further?

lines.speaker: Damian Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Damian Penner (Councillor) [medium]
lines.text: Uh, thank you, Mr. Mayor. There's, uh, there's not a lot of, uh, authority or power that we as municipally elected officials have, but at the same time, we do have a voice, and we have a voice that we should, uh, rise up and, and make sure is heard when there's citizens and local businesses that are, that are wanting To hear our voice. I hear— pardon me, I live right underneath the flight circuit of Harv's Air, and I can— I'm actually surprised that it's only 150 times a day on average that they say that they're going to fly over here, because it is a very busy airport. This isn't just some casual farmer that's going out for an evening flight. This airport is going— airport air school is going nonstop, almost 12 hours a day, if not longer, when they're doing their night training. And if this— if Mr. Penner has seen that this is going to be an issue, his business has been here much longer than the cell tower, which hasn't— doesn't have a foundation yet. So I think the precedent should go towards him, and I feel like it's appropriate for the City of Steinbach's voice to echo his concerns.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you. Councillor Siemens.

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, sir. I agree with, with the motion and the comments made. The— this is a A piece of Steinbach. This has been part of Steinbach for the last 50 years. And so, but, and many planes, many pilots. So they are part of our economic engine, so to speak, of Steinbach. I'm also very surprised that Transport Canada, or NavCan, and the CRTC don't talk to each other. They're 2 federal organizations that would play a critical role in both of these, and I think it's important that when you look at towers, that they're marked properly. And I'm not a pilot, but every once in a while when pilots talk about the structures that are in play in various places and what that controls, it's amazing that it's got to this point and that one of the busiest airports in southeastern Manitoba and probably could be in many Busier than many parts of Canada, but the— that there wasn't more discussion and more of an impact study done in some form. So absolutely, we need to send a letter of support.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you. Go ahead, Councillor Hiebert.

lines.speaker: Jake Hiebert
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jake Hiebert (Councillor)
lines.text: I do. Thank you, Mr. Mayor. I too agree with the comments that have been made, and I too find it interesting that Transport Canada and other government agencies would have entertained a tower of this height and size in this location. I'm familiar with Harv's Air, and they don't only have students from Steinbach, from Manitoba or Canada, North America. They have student— international students from all over the world that are flying here. And to have a tower that close to an airport that is that busy, it doesn't seem rational. So, you know, safety concerns are paramount and And like Councillor Siemens has said, it's— they're an integral part of our community. So I appreciate the comments by Councillor Zwaagstra in writing a letter in support of Harv's Air, that this is not an appropriate location for a tower of this size. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further? Anything in closing? Well, council, I believe that this is a good idea. I think this is so support for a business. In reality, the top portion of their, like the northern portion of their runway is in Steinbach, in the city of Steinbach. The rest of the business is in the arm of Hanover, but I think it's very important that we represent a Steinbach business 'cause they are in our, They're in our community. There is a great economic spinoff with the pilots that come. They all live in our community. And I think it's important that we show our support to this and that we help out in this way. And because all businesses in Steinbach are important to us. It is. It's what drives our engine. It gives us our growth and it helps us continue to move into the future. And so although we have— we don't have a lot of say in where these towers go, this is a federal decision, we do— we are allowed to comment. We can be a commenting agent and in a way to write a letter in support and break out and itemize the The challenges we have with this is the way to comment in this case. So call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. Thank you. There's no other business. Looking for a motion to adjourn. Councillor Penner, seconded by Councillor Hiebert. Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. Next council meeting is Tuesday, October 1st, 2024, at 7:30. Thank you.
